summary: The Controller host page shows a light beside the host's Nex Core version: pulsing green when it matches the newest release in the update archive, orange when a newer release exists, red when that is a new major release, with a hover explanation. GET /api/v1/updates additionally reports core_available_version. API impact: changed contract (additive field).

guide.reason: docs/guide/manage-controller.md describes the light's colours, the hover text and when no light appears.

api.reason: Controller GET /api/v1/updates gains the optional core_available_version field (newest nex-core-local in the archive); no request, authorization or Core-side contract changes. docs/API.md and docs/api/openapi.json updated.

roadmap.reason: Small UI addition within shipped host inventory and update behaviour.

state.reason: Nothing durable: the Controller reads the archive's index through its existing APT cache and compares it with the version each host already reports.

verification.method: go test ./internal/controller -run TestUpdatesAuthAndApply (asserts core_available_version); web/src/updates.test.mjs covers current, behind, major, ahead-of-archive and unknown; npm --prefix web run typecheck; generate_api.py --check. Browser (simulated, labelled): Playwright Chromium against a real Controller with the simulated agent, GET /api/v1/updates answered by route interception with core_available_version 0.4.3, 0.4.4, 1.4.3 and absent against a host presenting Nex Core 0.4.3; the Version row showed green, orange, red and no light with the expected hover titles and no page errors. No APT archive was read: this workstation has no apt, so the real archive lookup is untested here.
